memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"There will be loud wailing throughout Egypt-worse than there has ever been or
ever will be again." - Ex 11:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse describes grief, and it does not look away from it. Egypt would weep
as it had never wept before.

It is worth remembering that this sorrow began in Egypt's own choices. There was
a cry before this one. Exodus 3:7 records God saying, "I have indeed seen the
misery of my people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out." For four hundred
years, Israelite mothers had wailed over sons taken from them. Egypt had not
listened. Now Egypt would cry, and Pharaoh's hardened heart had brought his
nation there.

God is not casual about human suffering, including Egyptian suffering. Ezekiel
33:11 tells us plainly that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked.
But sin is not a small thing, and He does not pretend it is.

There is a third cry we should remember. On a hill outside Jerusalem, a Son
cried out and a Father did not turn away the judgment (Matt 27:46). That cry was
so that ours could end.

If you are in a season of weeping, know that God hears. He has never once
ignored a cry that came to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does the reality of judgment move you to pray for people who do not know
   Christ?
2. Is there a cry you need to bring to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You hear every cry. Thank You that Jesus bore the cry of judgment in my
place. Give me a tender heart for those who do not yet know You. Amen.
